messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected in us-east and midwest gateways (probable ingress surge). P50 latency spike and increased 502/504s. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
maria: seeing the same on dashboards — ingress pool errors spiking around 11:12 UTC. Keystone egress looks fine. Routing shows retries to midwest pool.
jordan: I’m taking lead. oncall-nyc are you awake? @oncall-nyc
oncall-nyc: here, woke up. I’ve pulled the runbook: `ingress-failure-staging` and starting checklist.
lee: quick note — synthetic traffic shows request timeouts hitting upstream LB in us-east-1a. Could be partial AZ saturation.
maria: binding logs from gateway show lots of `connection-reset-by-peer` and `upstream timeout` between 11:12-11:18. sample:
```
[11:15:22] gateway-1 us-east1a -> upstream: 504 read timeout (kvcache stalled)
[11:15:23] gateway-3 midwest -> upstream: 502 connection reset
```
```
netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l -> 4800 (baseline 1200)
```
jordan: odds are we have a fanout causing K/V cache backpressure on midwest cache nodes. Maria, can you check kvcache TTL evictions and queue depth?
maria: running `kgctl metrics --service=kvcache --pool=midwest --last=10m` — TTL evictions jump at 11:13, inflight queue depth > 95%.
ops-liz: I'm seeing autoscaler thrash in midwest: several scale-ups failed due to failed image pull in one nodegroup (a3b). That would explain capacity holes.
kevin-cs: we have 12 customer-reported errors in the last 5m — mostly webhooks failing with 502. CS is notifying top 10 affected accounts.
oncall-nyc: action plan: (1) divert new traffic away from midwest pool via route-steer to us-west fallback, (2) manually cordon problematic nodes in midwest to speed up replacement, (3) open fast-roll to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive paths. Any objections?
lee: +1 for steer. We should set a gradual steer so we don't overload us-west. Suggest 30% initial reroute.
jordan: doing route change now. `routesctl set-weight --from=ingress --pool=midwest --weight=0.7 --until=11:23UTC` then decrease to 0.3 — moving 30% to us-west. will monitor.
incident-bot: ROUTE CHANGE: weight update applied by jordan at 11:19 UTC. midwest weight -> 0.7. Broadcast to edge proxies.
maria: confirming decreased QPS to midwest, queue depth dropping slowly. 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 9% in 3 minutes.
ops-liz: cordoned nodegroup a3b. replacing nodes; kube shows pending pods stuck due to image pull error — I'm pushing a retry to registry and verifying connectivity.
kevin-cs: drafting customer comms: short note about partial regional degradation and failover with ETA for update in 30m.
lee: on perf — we triggered KV TTL fallback which caused some users to get slightly higher latency. Suggest we enable local prefix caching to reduce repeated warmups: `feature-flag:cold-cache-stub -> enable` for midwest.
jordan: enabling local cache stub now. `ffctl enable cold-cache-stub --scope=ingress.midwest`.
incident-bot: FEATURE FLAG: cold-cache-stub enabled by jordan (11:22 UTC).
maria: after cache stub, upstream hits dropped 40% and error rate is down to 4.2%. Good improvement.
oncall-nyc: still seeing sporadic 502s for long-tail customers. Suggest escalate to full traffic shift if errors trend upward. Current plan hold: keep 30% diverted, continue cordon/replace.
lee: monitoring heap and fd usage on gateway instances — no leak detected, but one midwest redis instance shows high CPU and network stalls. Could be a bad node causing backpressure.
jordan: opened ticket to infra: INFRA-8472 flagged the failing redis node. infra to replace.
ops-liz: registry issue fixed; new pods starting healthy. node replacement in progress.
kevin-cs: CS wants an ETA to share: any sense? oncall-nyc?
oncall-nyc: if replacements proceed, we should be at steady-state in ~18-25 minutes. I'll mark public status as partial outage in affected region and link this thread.
maria: planning to run a canary rollback if midwest doesn't stabilize — rollback ingress binary to previous build that had lower connection concurrency. That buys time if redis replacement lags.
jordan: agree. For now keep gradual steer and monitor error budget. If 5xx > 5% for 10m, escalate to full 70% reroute to us-west and page SRE-leads.
oncall-nyc: noted. Alerting threshold set.
incident-bot: UPDATE: 11:33 UTC — 5xx rate now 2.1% across global, midwest 3.8%. Routing and cache stub holding. Incident status: mitigation engaged; oncall managing replacement. Next update in 15m or on major change.
kevin-cs: sending interim update to customers now. thanks team.
maria: leaving a short postmortem checklist in #postmortems — will collect logs and timeline after incident. tagging `runbook:ingress-partial-failover`.
jordan: thanks all. handing to follow-on shift. @sre-rotation-bot please take post-incident ops and ensure runbook items are completed.
sre-rotation-bot: Acknowledged. Taking ownership for cleanup and write-up. Will schedule RCA meeting.
ops-liz: replacing redis node done. pods stable. Gradual de-steer to midwest planned at 11:44 UTC if no regression.
oncall-nyc: confirm final check: 5xx < 1% for 10m, QPS normalized. Proceeding to move weight back from 0.3 -> 1.0 midwest over 5 minutes.
jordan: applied weight ramp to 1.0. Monitoring.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: 11:45 UTC — routing restored to normal, midwest healthy. Incident closed for now. Postmortem owner: maria.
